    - heading "Why Nexoris Technologies exists." [level=2]
    - paragraph: Too much business software forces people to work around it. Staff keep a spreadsheet on the side because the system cannot do what they need. Managers wait days for numbers the business already has. Owners pay for tools the team quietly stopped using months ago.
    - paragraph: We started Nexoris Technologies to do the opposite. We begin with the problem and the people, and only then choose the technology. We take time to understand how your business actually runs, design the solution carefully, and build software that is reliable, easy to maintain, and fully owned by you at the end.
    - paragraph: The company is founded and led by Chinedu Nwogu, who works directly on every project from planning through to delivery. Our team combines modern software development practices with a clear understanding of the Nigerian business environment, including compliance requirements, local payment systems, and the way businesses here operate day to day. The result is software that performs well and that people can use without difficulty.

    - generic: Our delivery process
    - heading "Plan properly. Design before building. Check the work at every stage." [level=1]
    - paragraph: Whether the project is a single website or a full business platform, our process stays the same. We take time to understand the problem, design the solution carefully, and build software that is reliable, easy to maintain, and fully owned by you at the end.
    - link "Book a scoping call →":

  - region "The six stages":
    - generic: The process
    - heading "The six stages of every project." [level=2]
    - article:
      - generic: "01"
      - generic: Stage 01
      - heading "Discovery and Planning" [level=3]
      - paragraph: We start by understanding the business, its users, and any constraints. We ask a lot of questions, and we listen more than we talk. This stage produces a clear plan, scope, and timeline before development begins, so both sides know exactly what is being built, by when, and for how much.
    - article:
      - generic: "02"
      - generic: Stage 02
      - heading "UX/UI Design" [level=3]
      - paragraph: We create wireframes and full designs and have them reviewed with you before development starts. You see the product on screen and approve it before serious engineering money is spent. Changing a design costs little. Changing built software costs a lot. We do the changing here.
    - article:
      - generic: "03"
      - generic: Stage 03
      - heading "Development" [level=3]
      - paragraph: We build the product in stages using modern tools, and we keep you updated on progress throughout. You will never go weeks wondering what is happening. If something shifts, you hear it from us first, with options.
    - article:
      - generic: "04"
      - generic: Stage 04
      - heading "Quality Assurance and Testing" [level=3]
      - paragraph: We test across browsers and devices, and we check performance before any stage is marked complete. The product has to work for your real users on their real phones and connections, not just on our machines.
    - article:
      - generic: "05"
      - generic: Stage 05
      - heading "Deployment and Handover" [level=3]
      - paragraph: We deploy the finished product, provide documentation, and train your team where needed, so they can run the platform on their own. All source code, designs, and project files are handed over. Nothing is held back.
    - article:
      - generic: "06"
      - generic: Stage 06
      - heading "Ongoing Support" [level=3]
      - paragraph: We offer maintenance plans that cover updates, monitoring, and small improvements after launch. Most clients stay with us on one, because software that nobody maintains slowly becomes a problem.
  - region "What you can hold us to":
    - generic: Our commitments
    - heading "What you can hold us to." [level=2]
    - paragraph: A written scope, timeline, and cost before work begins.
    - paragraph: Straight answers when something changes, even when it is not what you expected to hear.
    - paragraph: Direct access to the people building your product.
    - paragraph: At the end, all source code, designs, and project files handed over to you. Nothing is held back, and there is no quiet dependency designed to keep you paying.
  - region "Ways to work":
    - generic: Engagement models
    - heading "Three ways to work with us." [level=2]
    - article:
      - heading "A project with a fixed written scope" [level=3]
      - generic: Best when you know what you need
      - paragraph: Best when you know what you need and want a clear price and date for it. We scope it, agree it in writing, and deliver it in stages you can see.
    - article:
      - heading "An ongoing product partnership" [level=3]
      - generic: Best for products that keep evolving
      - paragraph: Best when you are building something that will keep evolving, like a startup product or a growing platform. We work as your technical team over time, planning and shipping in regular cycles.
    - article:
      - heading "A managed operations plan" [level=3]
      - generic: Best after launch
      - paragraph: Best after launch. We monitor, update, support, and improve your platform on a monthly plan, so it keeps earning instead of going stale.
  - region "Who we serve best":
    - generic: Who we serve best
    - heading "Where we do our best work." [level=2]
    - article:
      - heading "Growing businesses of 50 to 1,000 staff" [level=3]
      - paragraph: You have outgrown spreadsheets, informal processes, and off-the-shelf tools that almost fit. You need custom systems, dashboards, or apps for your team and customers, built around how you actually operate.
    - article:
      - heading "Funded startups" [level=3]
      - paragraph: You have raised money and need a senior technical partner to build or rebuild your product, add the right intelligent features, and get the system ready for more users. We move at startup speed without startup shortcuts.
    - article:
      - heading "Larger companies modernising old systems" [level=3]
      - paragraph: You have legacy platforms that work but hold you back. We connect them, extend them, or replace them in stages, without stopping the business while we do it.
    - article:
      - heading "Public sector and development organisations" [level=3]
      - paragraph: You are building citizen services, revenue systems, or programme platforms, and you carry procurement and compliance requirements most vendors underestimate. We understand that world and design for it from the start.

    - paragraph: At Nexoris Technologies Ltd ("Nexoris", "we", "us", or "our"), we respect your privacy and are committed to protecting personal data entrusted to us.
    - paragraph: This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, disclose, store, protect, and otherwise process personal data when you visit our website, contact us, request our services, communicate with us, subscribe to our communications, interact with Nexoris Technologies Insights, apply for a position, or otherwise interact with Nexoris.
    - paragraph: It also explains your rights in relation to your personal data and how you can exercise those rights.
    - paragraph: This Privacy Policy should be read together with our Terms of Service, Cookies Policy, and any additional privacy or data-processing terms that may apply to a particular Nexoris service or client engagement.
    - heading "About Nexoris Technologies" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Nexoris Technologies Ltd is a technology company that designs, develops, integrates, deploys, and supports digital products and technology solutions for businesses and organisations.
    - paragraph: "Our services may include:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: AI-Powered Digital Product Development
      - paragraph: AI Chatbots & Virtual Assistants
      - paragraph: Intelligent Workflow & Business Process Automation
      - paragraph: AI Integration & System Connectivity
      - paragraph: Data Dashboards & Predictive Analytics
      - paragraph: Data Infrastructure & AI Readiness
      - paragraph: IoT Application Development & Integration
      - paragraph: AI-Powered E-Commerce & Digital Commerce
      - paragraph: GovTech & Public Sector Platforms
      - paragraph: AI Content, SEO & Generative Engine Optimisation
      - paragraph: Managed Technology Operations
    - paragraph: The personal data we process depends on how you interact with Nexoris and the nature of the services we provide.
    - heading "Scope of This Privacy Policy" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "This Privacy Policy applies to personal data processed by Nexoris through or in connection with:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: our website and digital properties;
      - paragraph: contact and enquiry forms;
      - paragraph: quotation and consultation requests;
      - paragraph: email, telephone, and other business communications;
      - paragraph: newsletter and marketing subscriptions;
      - paragraph: Nexoris Technologies Insights;
      - paragraph: recruitment and careers activities;
      - paragraph: business development activities;
      - paragraph: client and prospective-client engagements; and
      - paragraph: other services or digital properties that expressly refer to this Privacy Policy.
    - paragraph: Certain Nexoris services may have additional privacy notices, contractual provisions, or Data Processing Agreements. Where applicable, those additional terms will apply alongside this Privacy Policy.
    - heading "Who Is Responsible for Your Personal Data?" [level=2]
    - paragraph: For personal data that Nexoris processes for its own business purposes, Nexoris Technologies Ltd is responsible for determining how and why that personal data is processed.
    - paragraph: Where Nexoris processes personal data solely on behalf of a client as part of providing a technology service, the client may be the relevant data controller or equivalent responsible party, while Nexoris may act as a data processor or in another role recognised by applicable law.
    - paragraph: The respective responsibilities of Nexoris and the client in those circumstances will be determined by the applicable agreement and data-protection requirements.
    - heading "What Is Personal Data?" [level=2]
    - paragraph: For purposes of this Privacy Policy, personal data means information relating to an identified or identifiable individual.
    - paragraph: Personal data may include information that identifies you directly, as well as information that can reasonably be associated with you.
    - paragraph: Depending on how you interact with Nexoris, this may include your name, contact information, professional information, communications, technical information, and other information you choose to provide.
    - heading "Personal Data We May Collect" [level=2]
    - paragraph: The information we collect depends on your relationship with Nexoris.
    - heading "5.1 Information You Provide" [level=3]
    - paragraph: "You may provide personal data when you:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: contact us;
      - paragraph: submit an enquiry;
      - paragraph: request a quotation;
      - paragraph: request a consultation;
      - paragraph: submit a project brief;
      - paragraph: communicate with our team;
      - paragraph: subscribe to our communications;
      - paragraph: download or request a resource;
      - paragraph: apply for a position;
      - paragraph: participate in an event;
      - paragraph: enter into a business relationship with us; or
      - paragraph: otherwise voluntarily provide information.
    - paragraph: "This may include:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: full name;
      - paragraph: email address;
      - paragraph: telephone number;
      - paragraph: company or organisation;
      - paragraph: job title or professional role;
      - paragraph: business address;
      - paragraph: project requirements;
      - paragraph: information contained in correspondence;
      - paragraph: CV or résumé information;
      - paragraph: professional qualifications and experience;
      - paragraph: information provided during recruitment;
      - paragraph: information required to administer a client relationship; and
      - paragraph: other information reasonably necessary for the relevant purpose.
    - heading "5.2 Technical Information" [level=3]
    - paragraph: "When you interact with our website or certain digital services, we may receive technical information such as:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: IP address;
      - paragraph: browser type and version;
      - paragraph: operating system;
      - paragraph: device type;
      - paragraph: referring page or website;
      - paragraph: pages accessed;
      - paragraph: date and time of access;
      - paragraph: session information;
      - paragraph: technical diagnostics;
      - paragraph: website performance information; and
      - paragraph: security-related information.
    - paragraph: This information may be collected automatically through our systems or through service providers that support our website and digital infrastructure.
    - paragraph: For information about cookies and similar technologies specifically, please see our Cookies Policy.
    - heading "5.3 Information From Other Sources" [level=3]
    - paragraph: "Where appropriate and lawful, we may receive information about you from other sources, such as:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: your organisation;
      - paragraph: business partners;
      - paragraph: professional networks;
      - paragraph: publicly available business information;
      - paragraph: service providers;
      - paragraph: referrals; or
      - paragraph: other persons who are authorised to provide the information.
    - paragraph: We will process such information in accordance with applicable law and the purpose for which it was obtained.
    - heading "Why We Collect Personal Data" [level=2]
    - paragraph: We process personal data for legitimate and defined purposes.
    - paragraph: "Depending on the circumstances, we may use personal data to:"
    - heading "Respond to enquiries" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Respond to questions, project enquiries, quotation requests, consultation requests, and other communications.
    - heading "Provide our services" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Deliver, administer, support, maintain, and improve services provided to clients.
    - heading "Manage business relationships" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Communicate with clients, prospective clients, suppliers, contractors, partners, and other business contacts.
    - heading "Deliver projects" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Understand requirements, coordinate activities, manage deliverables, provide support, and perform contractual obligations.
    - heading "Communicate with you" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Send service-related, administrative, operational, and other communications relevant to our relationship.
    - heading "Send marketing communications" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Where permitted by applicable law and, where required, with your consent, send information about our services, insights, resources, events, and relevant company updates.
    - heading "Operate our website" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Maintain, secure, troubleshoot, and improve our website and digital properties.
    - heading "Improve our services" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Analyse feedback, usage patterns, technical information, and other relevant information to improve our services, content, products, and digital experiences.
    - heading "Maintain security" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Detect, investigate, prevent, and respond to security incidents, fraud, abuse, unauthorised activity, and threats to our systems.
    - heading "Recruitment" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Assess job applications, communicate with applicants, conduct interviews, and administer recruitment activities.
    - heading "Meet legal obligations" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Comply with applicable laws, regulations, lawful requests, court orders, regulatory requirements, and other legal obligations.
    - heading "Protect our rights" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Establish, exercise, or defend legal claims and protect the rights, property, systems, security, and legitimate interests of Nexoris and other persons.
    - heading "7. Lawful Bases for Processing" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Nexoris processes personal data only where an appropriate lawful basis exists under applicable data-protection law.
    - paragraph: "Depending on the circumstances, we may rely on:"
    - heading "Consent" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Where you have provided valid consent for a specified processing activity.
    - heading "Contract" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Where processing is necessary to enter into or perform a contract with you or your organisation.
    - heading "Legal obligation" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Where processing is necessary to comply with a legal or regulatory obligation.
    - heading "Vital interests" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Where processing is necessary to protect an individual's vital interests in circumstances recognised by applicable law.
    - heading "Public interest" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Where processing is necessary for a public-interest purpose or under applicable official authority.
    - heading "Legitimate interests" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Where permitted by applicable law and where our legitimate interests are not overridden by your applicable rights and interests.
    - paragraph: The lawful basis depends on the specific processing activity.
    - paragraph: Where processing is based on consent, you may withdraw that consent at any time. Withdrawal does not affect the lawfulness of processing carried out before consent was withdrawn.
    - heading "How We Use Personal Data" [level=2]
    - paragraph: We use personal data only for purposes that are compatible with the reason it was collected, another lawful purpose permitted by applicable law, or a purpose for which you have otherwise been appropriately informed.
    - paragraph: We do not use personal data for unrelated purposes merely because we have access to it.
    - paragraph: Where a new use is materially different from the original purpose, we will take appropriate steps required by applicable law before undertaking that processing.
    - heading "Data Minimisation" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Nexoris seeks to collect personal data that is adequate, relevant, and reasonably necessary for the purpose for which it is processed.
    - paragraph: We do not intentionally collect personal information simply because it may be useful at some point in the future.
    - paragraph: Where personal data is no longer necessary for the relevant purpose, it will be handled in accordance with our retention practices and applicable law.
    - heading "Accuracy of Personal Data" [level=2]
    - paragraph: We take reasonable steps to ensure that personal data under our control is accurate and, where necessary, kept reasonably up to date.
    - paragraph: You may contact us if information we hold about you is inaccurate or incomplete.
    - paragraph: Where appropriate, we will correct or update the information.
    - heading "Marketing Communications" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "Where permitted by applicable law, Nexoris may send marketing communications about:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: our services;
      - paragraph: technology insights;
      - paragraph: articles and guides;
      - paragraph: events;
      - paragraph: reports and resources;
      - paragraph: product or service updates; and
      - paragraph: other relevant business information.
    - paragraph: Where consent is required, we will obtain consent before sending the relevant marketing communications.
    - paragraph: You may unsubscribe at any time by using the unsubscribe option provided in the communication or by contacting us.
    - paragraph: Unsubscribing from marketing communications does not necessarily stop important service-related, transactional, security, or administrative communications.
    - heading "Nexoris Technologies Insights" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Nexoris publishes educational, technical, and professional content through Nexoris Technologies Insights.
    - paragraph: When you access or interact with our Insights content, we may process information necessary to operate the publication, understand engagement, provide requested resources, or administer subscriptions where applicable.
    - paragraph: Our Insights content may include links to external websites and resources.
    - paragraph: Those external websites operate independently and have their own privacy practices. Nexoris is not responsible for the privacy practices of third-party websites.
    - paragraph: Where an article or resource contains a form, subscription mechanism, download, or other interactive feature, the relevant collection of personal data will be governed by this Privacy Policy unless a separate privacy notice is provided.
    - heading "Recruitment and Careers" [level=2]
    - paragraph: If you apply for a position with Nexoris, we may collect information necessary to assess and manage your application.
    - paragraph: "This may include:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: name and contact information;
      - paragraph: CV or résumé;
      - paragraph: employment history;
      - paragraph: education;
      - paragraph: professional qualifications;
      - paragraph: skills and experience;
      - paragraph: portfolio or work samples;
      - paragraph: references;
      - paragraph: interview information; and
      - paragraph: other information you voluntarily provide during recruitment.
    - paragraph: "We use recruitment information to:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: assess suitability for available roles;
      - paragraph: communicate with candidates;
      - paragraph: conduct interviews and assessments;
      - paragraph: verify information where appropriate;
      - paragraph: manage the recruitment process; and
      - paragraph: meet applicable legal or administrative requirements.
    - paragraph: Recruitment information will not be used for unrelated purposes unless permitted by applicable law or supported by an appropriate lawful basis.
    - heading "Client Data" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Nexoris may process personal data contained within client systems, applications, databases, platforms, documents, or other environments while providing contracted technology services.
    - paragraph: Where that data belongs to or is controlled by a client, Nexoris generally processes it only for the purposes authorised by the client and the applicable agreement.
    - paragraph: Depending on the circumstances, Nexoris may act as a data processor or another relevant role under applicable data-protection law.
    - paragraph: "The client's instructions, the applicable Statement of Work, Master Services Agreement, Data Processing Agreement, and other contractual terms may establish specific requirements concerning:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: the categories of personal data processed;
      - paragraph: processing purposes;
      - paragraph: permitted processing activities;
      - paragraph: security measures;
      - paragraph: retention;
      - paragraph: deletion;
      - paragraph: international transfers;
      - paragraph: sub-processors;
      - paragraph: breach notification;
      - paragraph: data-subject requests; and
      - paragraph: other data-protection responsibilities.
    - paragraph: Where such contractual terms apply, they will govern the relevant client engagement.
    - heading "Sensitive Personal Data" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Nexoris does not generally seek sensitive personal data through its public website.
    - paragraph: You should not submit sensitive personal information through general enquiry forms unless the information is specifically requested and there is an appropriate reason and lawful basis for collecting it.
    - paragraph: Where a specific technology service requires the processing of sensitive or specially protected personal data, additional safeguards and contractual requirements may apply.
    - heading "Children and Minors" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Our general website and professional services are not directed primarily at children.
    - paragraph: We do not knowingly seek to collect personal data from children through our public website where such collection is not appropriate or legally permitted.
    - paragraph: Where a particular Nexoris project involves children or minors, additional privacy and safeguarding requirements may apply.
    - paragraph: If you believe that a child has provided personal data to Nexoris in circumstances where it should not have been collected, please contact us.
    - heading "Sharing Personal Data" [level=2]
    - paragraph: We may disclose personal data where reasonably necessary for the purposes described in this Privacy Policy and where an appropriate lawful basis exists.
    - paragraph: "Depending on the circumstances, recipients may include:"
    - heading "Employees and authorised personnel" [level=3]
    - paragraph: People within Nexoris who require access to perform their responsibilities.
    - heading "Contractors and consultants" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Individuals or organisations supporting our business or delivering services on our behalf.
    - heading "Technology and service providers" [level=3]
    - paragraph: "Providers supporting functions such as:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: hosting;
      - paragraph: cloud infrastructure;
      - paragraph: email;
      - paragraph: communications;
      - paragraph: analytics;
      - paragraph: cybersecurity;
      - paragraph: data storage;
      - paragraph: software;
      - paragraph: customer relationship management;
      - paragraph: project management;
      - paragraph: payment processing;
      - paragraph: AI services; and
      - paragraph: other business operations.
    - heading "Professional advisers" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Lawyers, accountants, auditors, consultants, insurers, and other professional advisers.
    - heading "Government and regulatory authorities" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Courts, regulators, law-enforcement agencies, government bodies, or other authorities where disclosure is required or permitted by law.
    - heading "Business transaction parties" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Where reasonably necessary in connection with a merger, acquisition, restructuring, financing, sale of assets, or similar corporate transaction.
    - paragraph: We seek to ensure that third parties who process personal data on our behalf are subject to appropriate contractual, technical, and organisational safeguards.
    - heading "Third-Party Service Providers" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Nexoris uses third-party technologies and service providers to operate our business and provide certain services.
    - paragraph: "Depending on the relevant activity, these may include providers of:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: cloud infrastructure;
      - paragraph: hosting;
      - paragraph: email and communications;
      - paragraph: analytics;
      - paragraph: cybersecurity;
      - paragraph: customer relationship management;
      - paragraph: payment processing;
      - paragraph: data storage;
      - paragraph: software development infrastructure;
      - paragraph: AI and machine-learning services; and
      - paragraph: other business technologies.
    - paragraph: The providers we use may change as our technology environment and business requirements evolve.
    - paragraph: Where a provider processes personal data on our behalf, we seek to ensure that appropriate contractual and security measures are in place.
    - heading "International Transfers" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Some third-party providers used by Nexoris may store or process personal data outside Nigeria.
    - paragraph: Where personal data is transferred outside Nigeria, Nexoris will take steps required by applicable data-protection law to ensure that the transfer is subject to appropriate safeguards.
    - paragraph: "Depending on the circumstances, these safeguards may include:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: appropriate contractual arrangements;
      - paragraph: assessment of the recipient and destination;
      - paragraph: applicable legal transfer mechanisms;
      - paragraph: security measures; and
      - paragraph: other safeguards required by applicable law.
    - heading "Data Retention" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Nexoris retains personal data only for as long as reasonably necessary for the purposes for which it was collected, unless a longer retention period is required or permitted by law.
    - paragraph: "The appropriate retention period may depend on:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: the nature of the personal data;
      - paragraph: the purpose for which it was collected;
      - paragraph: the existence of an ongoing relationship;
      - paragraph: contractual obligations;
      - paragraph: legal and regulatory requirements;
      - paragraph: accounting and tax requirements;
      - paragraph: dispute resolution;
      - paragraph: security considerations;
      - paragraph: legitimate business requirements; and
      - paragraph: applicable limitation periods.
    - paragraph: When personal data is no longer required, we will take reasonable steps to delete, securely destroy, anonymise, or otherwise dispose of it, subject to applicable legal and operational requirements.
    - heading "Data Security" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Nexoris takes reasonable technical and organisational measures appropriate to the nature and risk of the personal data we process.
    - paragraph: "Depending on the circumstances, these measures may include:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: access controls;
      - paragraph: authentication controls;
      - paragraph: role-based permissions;
      - paragraph: encryption where appropriate;
      - paragraph: secure development practices;
      - paragraph: security monitoring;
      - paragraph: backup and recovery controls;
      - paragraph: vulnerability management;
      - paragraph: security testing;
      - paragraph: confidentiality obligations;
      - paragraph: incident-response procedures; and
      - paragraph: periodic review of security measures.
    - paragraph: No electronic system or method of internet transmission can be guaranteed to be completely secure.
    - paragraph: Accordingly, while we take reasonable measures to protect personal data, we cannot guarantee absolute security.
    - heading "Personal Data Breaches" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Nexoris maintains procedures for responding to suspected or confirmed personal-data breaches.
    - paragraph: If we become aware of a breach involving personal data for which Nexoris is responsible, we will assess the incident and take appropriate steps in accordance with applicable law.
    - paragraph: Where notification to a regulatory authority or affected individual is legally required, we will make the relevant notification within the applicable timeframe.
    - paragraph: Where Nexoris processes personal data on behalf of a client, the applicable contractual arrangements and law will determine the respective responsibilities of Nexoris and the client for assessing, reporting, and responding to the incident.
    - heading "Privacy by Design" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Nexoris seeks to consider privacy and data protection when designing and implementing technology systems.
    - paragraph: "Where appropriate, this may include:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: limiting data collection;
      - paragraph: applying access controls;
      - paragraph: considering data retention;
      - paragraph: implementing appropriate security measures;
      - paragraph: separating environments and permissions;
      - paragraph: documenting processing requirements;
      - paragraph: considering privacy risks during product design; and
      - paragraph: incorporating appropriate safeguards into technical architecture.
    - paragraph: Where Nexoris is developing a technology solution for a client, privacy requirements may form part of the project's technical, security, or compliance requirements.
    - heading "Artificial Intelligence and Automated Processing" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Nexoris may use artificial intelligence and automated technologies in certain business activities and technology services.
    - paragraph: Where personal data is processed through AI or automated systems, Nexoris will apply safeguards appropriate to the nature and risk of the processing and applicable law.
    - paragraph: We do not intend to use personal data collected through this website to train publicly available AI models unless there is an appropriate lawful basis for doing so and, where required, appropriate notice or consent has been provided.
    - paragraph: "Where a client engages Nexoris to design, develop, integrate, or operate an AI-enabled system, the applicable agreement may contain additional requirements concerning:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: data processing;
      - paragraph: model providers;
      - paragraph: human oversight;
      - paragraph: security;
      - paragraph: retention;
      - paragraph: model use;
      - paragraph: monitoring;
      - paragraph: accuracy;
      - paragraph: acceptable use; and
      - paragraph: automated decision-making.
    - heading "Data Subject Rights" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Subject to applicable law and any applicable exemptions or limitations, you may have rights concerning your personal data.
    - paragraph: "These may include the right to:"
    - heading "Be informed" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Receive clear information about how your personal data is processed.
    - heading "Access" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Request access to personal data held about you and information concerning its processing.
    - heading "Rectification" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Request correction of inaccurate or incomplete personal data.
    - heading "Erasure" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Request deletion of personal data where the applicable legal conditions for erasure are satisfied.
    - heading "Restriction" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Request restriction of certain processing in circumstances recognised by applicable law.
    - heading "Object" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Object to certain types of processing where the applicable legal conditions are satisfied.
    - heading "Data portability" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Where applicable, request personal data in a structured, commonly used, and machine-readable format or request its transfer to another organisation.
    - heading "Withdraw consent" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Where processing is based on consent, withdraw that consent at any time.
    - heading "Rights relating to automated decision-making" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Where applicable, exercise rights concerning decisions based solely on automated processing that produce legal or similarly significant effects.
    - paragraph: These rights are subject to applicable legal conditions and are not necessarily absolute.
    - heading "Exercising Your Privacy Rights" [level=2]
    - paragraph: To exercise a data-protection right or make a privacy request, contact us using the details provided in the Contact Us section below.
    - paragraph: "To help us process your request efficiently, you should provide, where reasonably possible:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: your name;
      - paragraph: contact details;
      - paragraph: the nature of your request;
      - paragraph: information concerning the personal data or processing involved; and
      - paragraph: any other information reasonably necessary to verify and process the request.
    - paragraph: We may request reasonable information to verify your identity before fulfilling certain requests.
    - paragraph: This is intended to protect your personal data from unauthorised disclosure.
    - paragraph: We will respond to valid requests within the timeframe required by applicable law.
    - heading "Complaints" [level=2]
    - paragraph: If you have concerns about how Nexoris processes your personal data, we encourage you to contact us first so that we can investigate and attempt to resolve the matter.
    - paragraph: Where applicable, you may also lodge a complaint with the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) or another competent supervisory authority.
    - paragraph: Nothing in this Privacy Policy prevents you from exercising any statutory right to complain to a competent data-protection authority.
    - heading "Third-Party Websites" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Our website and digital properties may contain links to third-party websites, applications, platforms, or resources.
    - paragraph: Those third parties operate independently of Nexoris.
    - paragraph: A link does not mean that Nexoris endorses or controls the third party or its privacy practices.
    - paragraph: We encourage you to review the privacy policy of any third-party website or service before providing personal information.
    - heading "Social Media" [level=2]

    - paragraph: This Cookies Policy explains how Nexoris Technologies Ltd ("Nexoris", "we", "us", or "our") uses cookies and similar technologies when you visit or interact with our website and other digital properties that link to this policy.
    - paragraph: This policy explains what cookies are, why we use them, the types of cookies that may be used, how third parties may use similar technologies on our website, and the choices available to you.
    - paragraph: This Cookies Policy should be read together with our Privacy Policy and Terms of Service.
    - heading "What Are Cookies?" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Cookies are small text files that websites may place on your browser or device when you visit a website.
    - paragraph: They allow a website to recognise a browser or device and can help the website remember information, provide functionality, understand how visitors use the website, maintain security, or support other legitimate purposes.
    - paragraph: "Cookies may be:"
    - heading "First-party cookies" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Cookies placed directly by Nexoris or by technologies operating on our behalf.
    - heading "Third-party cookies" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Cookies or similar technologies placed or operated by third-party providers whose services are integrated into our website.
    - paragraph: "Cookies may also be classified according to how long they remain on your device:"
    - heading "Session cookies" [level=3]
    - paragraph: These generally remain on your device only while your browsing session is active and are removed when the session ends or the browser is closed.
    - heading "Persistent cookies" [level=3]
    - paragraph: These remain on your device for a defined period or until you delete them.
    - heading "Why Nexoris Uses Cookies" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "Depending on how our website is configured, we may use cookies and similar technologies for purposes including:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: keeping the website functioning properly;
      - paragraph: maintaining security;
      - paragraph: remembering preferences;
      - paragraph: understanding website usage;
      - paragraph: measuring website performance;
      - paragraph: improving website content and functionality;
      - paragraph: diagnosing technical problems;
      - paragraph: supporting communications and marketing activities where applicable; and
      - paragraph: protecting the website against abuse or unauthorised activity.
    - paragraph: We aim to use cookies only where they serve a defined and legitimate purpose.
    - heading "Categories of Cookies We May Use" [level=2]
    - paragraph: The specific cookies used on the Nexoris website may change as we introduce, remove, or update technologies.
    - paragraph: The main categories are described below.
    - heading "3.1 Strictly Necessary Cookies" [level=3]
    - paragraph: These cookies are necessary for certain website functions or security measures to operate.
    - paragraph: "They may be used to:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: maintain secure sessions;
      - paragraph: support essential website functionality;
      - paragraph: remember technical settings required for the website to operate;
      - paragraph: protect forms and interactions from abuse;
      - paragraph: maintain security; or
      - paragraph: provide functionality that you have specifically requested.
    - paragraph: Because these cookies may be necessary for the operation of the website, they may not always be capable of being disabled through our cookie-preference controls.
    - heading "3.2 Preference Cookies" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Preference cookies allow the website to remember choices you make.
    - paragraph: "Depending on the website functionality, these may include preferences relating to:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: language;
      - paragraph: display settings;
      - paragraph: interface preferences;
      - paragraph: form or session choices; or
      - paragraph: other customisations.
    - paragraph: Where applicable, these cookies are used to provide a more consistent and convenient experience.

    - paragraph: Where applicable law requires consent for these technologies, we will seek the appropriate consent before activating them.
    - heading "3.4 Marketing Cookies and Similar Technologies" [level=3]

      - paragraph: understand interactions with marketing content;
      - paragraph: help us determine whether a visitor has previously interacted with a campaign; or

    - paragraph: We will use these technologies only in accordance with applicable law and any required consent.
    - heading "3.5 Security and Fraud-Prevention Technologies" [level=3]

    - list:

      - paragraph: malicious traffic;

    - heading "Similar Technologies" [level=2]

      - paragraph: local storage;

      - paragraph: device identifiers;

    - paragraph: Where these technologies process personal data, they are also subject to our Privacy Policy and applicable data-protection requirements.
    - heading "Third-Party Cookies" [level=2]

    - paragraph: "These third parties may include providers of:"

      - paragraph: security services;
      - paragraph: embedded content;
      - paragraph: communication tools;
      - paragraph: marketing platforms;
      - paragraph: advertising services;

    - paragraph: Third-party providers may process information according to their own privacy policies and terms.
    - paragraph: Nexoris does not control the privacy practices of third parties.
    - paragraph: Where third-party technologies are used, we seek to ensure that their use is consistent with applicable legal and contractual requirements.
    - heading "Cookie Consent" [level=2]

      - paragraph: reject optional cookies;
      - paragraph: select specific categories;
      - paragraph: change your preferences later; or
      - paragraph: withdraw previously provided consent.
    - paragraph: Strictly necessary technologies may continue to operate where they are required for the website to function or for other purposes permitted by applicable law.
    - heading "Managing Your Cookie Preferences" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Where a cookie-preference mechanism is available on our website, you can use it to manage the categories of optional cookies that you permit.
    - paragraph: You can also manage cookies through your browser settings.
    - paragraph: "Most browsers allow you to:"
    - list:
      - paragraph: view stored cookies;
      - paragraph: delete existing cookies;
      - paragraph: block certain or all cookies;
      - paragraph: receive notifications before cookies are stored; and
      - paragraph: configure preferences for particular websites.
    - paragraph: Disabling certain cookies may affect how our website operates or prevent some functionality from working as intended.
    - paragraph: Browser controls differ depending on the browser and device you use.
    - heading "Withdrawing Consent" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Where processing of cookies or similar technologies is based on your consent, you may withdraw your consent at any time through the available cookie-preference mechanism, where provided.
    - paragraph: Withdrawing consent does not affect the lawfulness of processing that occurred before your withdrawal.
    - paragraph: If you withdraw consent for optional cookies, some website functionality or personalised features may be affected.
    - heading "Do Not Track Signals" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Some browsers and devices provide "Do Not Track" or similar privacy settings.
    - paragraph: Because there is currently no universally consistent technical standard for interpreting such signals across all websites and technologies, Nexoris may not respond to every browser-generated Do Not Track signal.
    - paragraph: Where applicable law requires us to recognise a particular privacy signal, we will do so in accordance with the applicable requirements.
    - heading "Cookies and Personal Data" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Some cookies may collect information that can be associated with an identifiable individual.
    - paragraph: Where this occurs, the information will be treated as personal data and processed in accordance with our Privacy Policy and applicable data-protection law.

    - paragraph: Analytics providers may process information according to their own terms and privacy policies.
    - heading "Cookies and Marketing" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Where marketing technologies are used, they may allow Nexoris to understand how visitors interact with marketing content or communications.
    - paragraph: Where required by applicable law, Nexoris will obtain consent before activating non-essential marketing cookies or similar technologies.
    - paragraph: You may withdraw or change your preferences through the available cookie controls.
    - heading "Legal Basis" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Where cookies or similar technologies involve the processing of personal data, the relevant processing will be conducted on an appropriate lawful basis under applicable data-protection law.
    - paragraph: "Depending on the purpose and circumstances, this may include:"
    - list:

      - paragraph: contractual necessity;
      - paragraph: legal obligation; or

  - heading "What does a website price actually include?" [level=2]
  - paragraph: "A website price in Nigeria covers three groups of costs: build, launch, and ongoing. The build is the design and development work. The launch is hosting, domain, SSL, content, and the SEO foundation. The ongoing is maintenance, security updates, and post-launch support."
  - paragraph: Build costs cover the design and user experience work, the actual development, and testing across phones, browsers, and slow connections. Launch costs cover hosting, the domain name, an SSL certificate, the words and images that go on the site, and the SEO setup that gives your pages a fair chance to rank.
  - paragraph: Ongoing costs cover maintenance, security patches, support, and any SEO or paid advertising you run after launch. When a quote feels too low, the reason is almost always that two or three of these line items are missing or will be charged separately later.
  - heading "What are the price ranges for different types of websites in Nigeria?" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: Website prices in Nigeria range from
    - strong: ₦200,000 for a basic WordPress business site to over ₦20,000,000 for a fully custom-coded fintech or healthcare platform
    - text: in 2026. A basic business site costs
    - strong: ₦200,000 to ₦500,000
    - text: . A mid-sized corporate site costs
    - strong: ₦500,000 to ₦1,500,000
    - text: .
  - paragraph:
    - text: A custom-coded marketing site costs
    - strong: ₦1,500,000 to ₦4,000,000
    - text: . An e-commerce store costs
    - strong: ₦800,000 to ₦3,000,000
    - text: . A
    - strong: custom platform or web application
    - text: costs
    - strong: ₦2,500,000 to ₦20,000,000
    - text: and up. Here is what each of those actually covers, and where the price moves within the range.
  - 'heading "Basic business website on WordPress: ₦200,000 to ₦500,000" [level=3]'
  - paragraph:
    - text: A basic business website built on WordPress in Nigeria costs
    - strong: ₦200,000 to ₦500,000
    - text: and covers three to five pages with home, about, services, contact, and one extra. Most of these are built using a clean template, light customisation, a contact form, and basic SEO setup. This option suits consultants, small service businesses, and any company that mainly needs a credible online presence.
  - paragraph:
    - text: At this price you should expect a mobile-responsive design, a working contact form, an SSL certificate, and
    - strong: basic on-page SEO
    - text: . You should not expect deep brand work, custom illustrations, or third-party integrations.
  - 'heading "Mid-sized corporate website: ₦500,000 to ₦1,500,000" [level=3]'
  - paragraph: A mid-sized corporate website costs ₦500,000 to ₦1,500,000 and typically covers ten to twenty pages, a content management system your team can actually use, a blog or insights section, structured data for SEO, and one or two integrations such as a CRM, an email platform, or a booking widget.
  - paragraph: Most of these are still built on WordPress in Nigeria, but with serious customisation and proper performance tuning. This is where most established Nigerian companies land once they take their website seriously. The extra money goes into design quality, content structure, performance tuning, and training your team to update the CMS without calling a developer every week.
  - paragraph: From the SEO work I led across African and international markets before founding Nexoris Technologies, including the Pixel Forge campaign that reached over 900 percent organic growth, the difference between a corporate site that ranks and one that does not usually shows up at this stage.
  - paragraph: Skipping the design and content structure here is a false saving, because poor user experience quietly wastes the money you spent on the rest of the site.
  - 'heading "Custom-coded marketing or business website: ₦1,500,000 to ₦4,000,000" [level=3]'
  - paragraph:
    - text: A fully custom-coded marketing website in Nigeria costs
    - strong: ₦1,500,000 to ₦4,000,000
    - text: in 2026. Custom-coded means the site is built from scratch using frameworks like Next.js, React, Vue, or similar, often with a headless CMS, instead of being assembled on top of WordPress or Wix.
  - paragraph: The lower end of the range is a 5 to 10 page site with a custom frontend and a simple content layer. The upper end includes bespoke animations, multiple language versions, complex page layouts, performance tuning, and serious SEO and accessibility work.
  - paragraph: Brands choose custom-coded over WordPress when they need real performance, design that templates cannot deliver, security or compliance that rules out third-party plugins, or a foundation that will grow into a product over the next two to three years. The trade-off is that custom-coded sites take 8 to 16 weeks to build instead of 4 to 8, and most updates need a developer rather than a member of your marketing team.
  - paragraph: About four in ten of the websites Nexoris Technologies delivered in 2025 were custom-coded, mostly for fintech, government, healthcare, and SaaS clients. WordPress was the right call for the other six. If your site is essentially a brochure with a contact form, custom-coding it is usually a waste of money.
  - 'heading "E-commerce store: ₦800,000 to ₦3,000,000" [level=3]'
  - paragraph:
    - text: An e-commerce website in Nigeria costs
    - strong: ₦800,000 to ₦3,000,000
    - text: and includes a product catalogue, secure checkout, a payment gateway, inventory management, order notifications, and an admin dashboard. The lower end of the range is a Shopify or WooCommerce setup with a polished theme.
  - paragraph: The higher end is a custom store with promotions, multi-vendor support, or integrated logistics. A fully custom-coded e-commerce platform sits above this range and can pass ₦8,000,000 for marketplaces.
  - paragraph:
    - text: Payments add their own costs. Paystack, Flutterwave, and Interswitch are the common Nigerian options. Developers typically charge
    - strong: ₦40,000 to ₦60,000
    - text: to wire these in properly, and the gateways themselves take a per-transaction fee. Paystack's standard local rate is 1.5 percent plus ₦100 per transaction.
  - paragraph: For context, well-known Nigerian platforms like Jumia and Konga sit far above this range because they are full marketplaces, not stores. A focused single-brand store like the ones we have built for fashion, food, and homeware clients sits squarely in the ₦1.2 million to ₦2.5 million bracket.
  - 'heading "Custom platform or web application: ₦2,500,000 to ₦20,000,000+" [level=3]'
  - paragraph: A custom platform or web application in Nigeria starts at ₦2,500,000 and can pass ₦20,000,000, because at this stage the work stops being a website and becomes software. Booking systems, learning platforms, member portals, internal dashboards, marketplaces, and fintech tools all sit here. Price depends almost entirely on scope and compliance requirements.
  - paragraph:
    - text: A simple booking system with a basic admin and Paystack integration might cost
    - strong: ₦2,500,000 to ₦4,000,000
    - text: . A multi-sided marketplace with payments, ratings, and search can run ₦8,000,000 to ₦15,000,000. A fintech platform with NDPA and PCI compliance, or a healthcare platform with patient data handling, can pass
    - strong: ₦20,000,000
    - text: .
  - paragraph: To picture the tier, think Glovo or Chowdeck for food delivery, Jiji for marketplaces, and SeamlessHR for SaaS-style platforms. None of those started at full scale. They started small and grew.
  - paragraph: This is also the stage where building in phases pays off. Most of the bank, manufacturer, and government clients we work with at Nexoris Technologies start with a focused version one and add features quarterly, because that approach is cheaper, faster, and closer to how real users actually behave once the platform is live.
  - heading "How much does a WordPress website cost in Nigeria?" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: A WordPress website in Nigeria costs between
    - strong: ₦150,000 and ₦1,500,000
    - text: in 2026, depending on whether you use a stock theme, a premium theme, or a heavily customised build. Roughly six in ten of the business sites Nexoris Technologies delivered in 2025 were built on WordPress, because it is flexible, well-supported, and easy to hand back to a client without locking them in.
  - paragraph:
    - text: A stock-theme site with light customisation costs
    - strong: ₦150,000 to ₦300,000
    - text: and works for very small businesses. A premium-theme build with proper performance tuning, plugin selection, and on-page SEO costs
    - strong: ₦400,000 to ₦800,000
    - text: and is the sweet spot for most SMEs.
  - paragraph: A heavily customised WordPress build with a bespoke theme, advanced custom fields, and integrations costs ₦800,000 to ₦1,500,000 and is the right call for companies that need control without paying for a fully custom-coded platform.
  - paragraph:
    - text: The thing nobody tells you about WordPress is that the platform itself is free, but the plugins are usually not. A real WordPress site typically runs three to five premium plugins, each costing $49 to $199 a year. At early-2026 exchange rates, that is
    - strong: ₦70,000 to ₦300,000
    - text: a year just in plugin renewals. Budget for it.
  - heading "How much does a custom-coded website cost in Nigeria?" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: A fully custom-coded website in Nigeria costs
    - strong: ₦1,500,000 to over ₦20,000,000
    - text: in 2026, depending on the scope. Custom-coded means the site is built from scratch using frameworks like Next.js, React, Vue, Laravel, Django, or Node.js, instead of being assembled on top of WordPress, Wix, or Shopify.
  - paragraph: About four in ten of the websites Nexoris Technologies delivered in 2025 were custom-coded, almost all of them for fintech, government, healthcare, and SaaS clients.
  - paragraph:
    - strong: "Here is roughly what custom-coded costs by project type in Nigeria:"
  - paragraph:
    - text: A custom-coded marketing or business site of 5 to 15 pages with a custom frontend and a headless CMS runs
    - strong: ₦1,500,000 to ₦4,000,000
    - text: . A custom-coded business platform with login, dashboards, and integrations runs
    - strong: ₦4,000,000 to ₦10,000,000
    - text: . A full SaaS or marketplace MVP runs
    - strong: ₦8,000,000 to ₦20,000,000
    - text: .
  - paragraph: A fintech, healthcare, or compliance-heavy platform starts at ₦15,000,000 and rises with the compliance scope. You should consider going custom-coded when off-the-shelf platforms genuinely cannot do what your site needs.
  - paragraph: The most common reasons are performance, security and compliance, bespoke design that templates cannot deliver, and product complexity that grows over time. If your site is essentially a brochure with a contact form, custom-coding it is usually the wrong call.
  - figure "WordPress will deliver the same visible result in a fraction of the time and budget.":
    - img "Nexoris Technologies comparison chart showing cost and timeline differences between WordPress and custom-coded builds in Nige"
    - generic: WordPress will deliver the same visible result in a fraction of the time and budget.
  - paragraph: Custom-coded sites take longer to build, typically 8 to 20 weeks for an MVP versus 4 to 10 weeks for WordPress, and need a developer to update most things. The benefit is that you own the codebase, the performance ceiling is far higher, and the platform can grow without hitting plugin limits.
  - heading "What recurring costs come with owning a website in Nigeria?" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: Owning a website in Nigeria costs between
    - strong: ₦80,000 and ₦2,000,000
    - text: per year after the build, depending on the size of the site and how active it is. The build gets all the attention. The recurring costs catch people out.
  - list:
    - strong: "Domain name:"
    - text: ₦3,000 to ₦25,000 per year for the common business extensions. Based on Go54's published rates in April 2026, a .com.ng renews at around ₦6,450, a .ng at around ₦15,000, and a .com at ₦24,000. Premium extensions like .ai cost much more, sometimes ₦200,000 and above.
    - strong: "Hosting:"
    - text: ₦20,000 to ₦500,000 per year. Shared hosting in Nigeria starts around ₦24,000 a year and works for small business sites. E-commerce, custom-coded sites, and high-traffic platforms belong on VPS or cloud hosting, which costs more but handles traffic spikes without the site going down.
    - strong: "SSL certificate:"
    - text: Free with Let's Encrypt on most modern hosts. Premium certificates with extended validation, useful for fintech and any platform handling cards, run ₦80,000 to ₦150,000 per year.
    - strong: "Maintenance:"
    - text: ₦50,000 to ₦200,000 per year for a basic business site. ₦150,000 to ₦400,000 per year for a mid-sized corporate site. ₦200,000 to ₦600,000 per year for an active e-commerce store. Custom platforms with active development can run ₦500,000 to ₦2,000,000 per year and beyond. Skipping maintenance is the most common reason Nigerian websites break, get hacked, or quietly lose traffic.
    - strong: "Content creation:"
    - text: ₦40,000 to over ₦1,000,000 per year if you publish regularly. Writers, photographers, and designers are not free.
    - strong: "SEO and paid ads:"
    - text: Separate from the build. Budget at least ₦100,000 per month if you want the site to bring in real leads. The Pixel Forge growth I led to over 900 percent did not happen because of the website alone. It happened because content and SEO ran every month, without stopping, for two years.
  - heading "What hidden costs do most Nigerian website quotes leave out?" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: "Most Nigerian website quotes leave out seven costs that show up later: VAT, dollar-priced plugins, professional email,"
    - strong: cybersecurity and NDPA-aligned data handling
    - text: ", premium SSL, content creation, and post-launch support. Together these can add"
    - strong: ₦300,000 to ₦1,500,000
    - text: per year on top of the build price.
  - list:
    - strong: "VAT at 7.5 percent:"
    - text: Web design services in Nigeria attract 7.5 percent VAT.
    - strong: On a ₦500,000 project, VAT adds ₦37,500
    - text: . Some agencies include this in the quoted price. Some add it to the invoice. Always ask whether the quote is VAT-inclusive before signing.
    - strong: "Dollar-priced plugins and tools:"
    - text: Many of the most useful WordPress plugins, page builders, form builders, membership systems, and SEO tools are priced in US dollars. A $99 per year plugin runs roughly ₦145,000 at early-2026 rates. Three or four of these add ₦400,000 to ₦600,000 per year that nobody mentioned in the original quote.
    - strong: "Professional email:"
    - text: Google Workspace or Zoho Mail costs ₦10,000 to ₦15,000 per user per year. Most quotes for the website itself leave email out. If your team is five people, that is another ₦60,000 to ₦75,000 a year.
    - strong: "NDPA compliance:"
    - text: The Nigeria Data Protection Act of 2023 affects any site that collects customer data, including e-commerce stores and any platform with user accounts. Privacy policy drafting, data processing agreements, and basic compliance setup typically run
    - strong: ₦100,000 to ₦500,000
    - text: . Larger platforms need annual audits, which cost more.
    - strong: "Premium SSL:"
    - text: Free SSL is fine for most sites. Banks, fintech, and any platform handling cards usually need extended validation certificates, which run ₦80,000 to ₦150,000 per year.
    - strong: "Content:"
    - text: Most quotes include the website but not the words on it. Writing, editing, and image sourcing for a ten-page site can run
    - strong: ₦100,000 to ₦400,000
    - text: if you do not have someone in-house.
    - strong: "Post-launch support:"
    - text: If the quote does not include a maintenance retainer, every fix after launch is billed separately. The first surprise invoice is usually within two months of launch.
  - figure:
    - img "A Nexoris Technologies website project quote document with purple sticky notes covering various service line items."
  - heading "How does Naira fluctuation affect website costs in Nigeria?" [level=2]
  - paragraph: Naira fluctuation pushes website costs up every year, because hosting, premium plugins, design tools, email services, and many SEO platforms are priced in US dollars. When the Naira weakens, your renewal bills rise even though nothing on your site has changed.
  - paragraph:
    - text: A hosting plan that cost
    - strong: ₦60,000 last year can become ₦90,000 this year
    - text: on the same plan. A $99 per year plugin that cost ₦120,000 to renew in 2024 ran closer to ₦150,000 in 2026. None of this is the developer's fault. It is currency exposure.
  - heading "Three ways to protect your budget" [level=3]
  - list:
    - strong: "Choose Naira-priced services where possible:"
    - text: Local hosting providers bill directly in Naira, so renewals are predictable.
    - strong: "Pay annually, not monthly:"
    - text: Annual plans usually lock in the rate and shield you from mid-year price changes.
    - strong: "Keep your tooling lean:"
    - text: Every dollar-priced plugin or service you add is one more line item exposed to currency risk. Use what you need. Remove what you do not.
  - heading "Does website cost in Nigeria differ between Lagos, Abuja, and Port Harcourt?" [level=2]
  - paragraph: Website costs in Nigeria differ between Lagos, Abuja, and Port Harcourt, but the gap is narrower than most buyers think. Lagos quotes for the same scope tend to run 10 to 25 percent higher than Abuja or Port Harcourt, mainly because the cost of running an agency in Lagos is higher.
  - paragraph: A basic business site that costs ₦300,000 in Port Harcourt typically runs ₦350,000 to ₦400,000 in Lagos for equivalent quality. The actual work is the same. The cost of the team doing it is not.
  - paragraph: Two notes worth flagging. First, geography matters less than it used to. Most decent Nigerian agencies, including Nexoris Technologies, work remotely with clients across all three cities and beyond, so location should not be the deciding factor. Second, the Lagos premium is real but inconsistent.
  - paragraph: A few Lagos agencies charge enterprise rates because they can. Others charge mid-market rates and do excellent work. Always compare three quotes regardless of city.
  - heading "Should I hire a freelancer, an agency, or use a DIY builder?" [level=2]
  - paragraph: A freelancer is cheapest, an agency gives you the most reliable result, and a DIY builder is best only if your budget is below ₦200,000 and you have time to learn. Each option fits a different situation.

  - heading "Why is cheap website design in Nigeria usually a bad deal?" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: Cheap website design in Nigeria, meaning anything below
    - strong: ₦100,000
    - text: for a multi-page business site, is usually a bad deal because the price can only be that low if the developer cuts corners on hosting, design quality, security, or ownership. The savings rarely last twelve months.
  - paragraph:
    - text: Here is what a
    - strong: ₦50,000 to ₦100,000 quote
    - text: almost always means in practice. The developer uses a free or pirated theme, often unsupported. Hosting is on the cheapest plan available, sometimes registered in their own name so you do not actually own the account.
  - paragraph: The domain may be registered in their name too, which means if you part ways, you can lose your web address. Maintenance is not included, so the first plugin conflict or security patch becomes a new bill. The SEO setup is missing, so the site is technically online but invisible.
  - paragraph:
    - text: Of the rebuild projects Nexoris Technologies took on in 2025, the average client had paid
    - strong: ₦80,000 to ₦150,000
    - text: for a first build, then paid us four to seven times that to rebuild it properly within two years. The cheap version is rarely the cheap option once you do the maths.
  - heading "How to spot a website quote that is too low" [level=2]
  - paragraph: A website quote in Nigeria is too low if it lacks a written scope, has no defined timeline, excludes post-launch support, or sits well below the ranges in this guide. A suspiciously low quote is a warning, not a bargain.
  - heading "The most common signals" [level=3]
  - list:
    - strong: No written contract or scope document.
    - text: If the agreement is verbal or limited to WhatsApp messages, you have no recourse if things go wrong.
    - strong: No defined timeline.
    - text: "\"We will start soon\" is not a timeline. Real quotes name dates and milestones."
    - strong: No mention of post-launch support.
    - text: Websites need updates. If support is not in the quote, you will be charged separately for every fix later.
    - strong: Prices well below the ranges in this guide.

  - 'heading "Hospital Management System in Nigeria: 2026 Buyer''s Guide" [level=2]'
  - paragraph:
    - img "Nigerian hospital owner and senior administrator reviewing hospital management system proposals and dashboard demo at a Lagos meeting room, weighing build versus buy options for 2026."
  - paragraph:
    - text: If you run a hospital, clinic, or
    - strong: HMO in Nigeria
    - text: and you are still working from paper files, scattered spreadsheets, or three software tools that do not share data, the question is not whether to digitise. It is what to choose, what it will actually cost, and how to avoid the kind of failed rollout that wastes 18 months and leaves your staff back on paper.
  - paragraph:
    - text: This guide gives you real prices, the rules you have to follow, the integrations that matter, and a clear
    - strong: way to decide between buying off-the-shelf and building custom
    - text: .
    - text: The costs and deployment patterns here come from healthcare projects delivered by
    - strong:
      - link "Nexoris Technologies":
        - /url: /
    - text: for Nigerian clients between 2025 and 2026.
  - paragraph:
    - text: Regulatory references draw on the
    - strong: National Health Insurance Authority Act 2022
    - text: ", the"
    - strong: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023
    - text: ", the"
    - strong: Federal Ministry of Health's National Digital Health Policy
    - text: ", the"
    - strong: HL7 FHIR specification
    - text: ", and the"
    - strong: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria's
    - text: telemedicine guidelines. NHIA reform figures reflect publicly reported announcements from February and April 2025.
  - 'heading "Quick Answer: What an HMS Costs in Nigeria in 2026" [level=2]'
  - paragraph:
    - text: A
    - strong: hospital management system (HMS)
    - text: is the central software that runs a Nigerian hospital, holding patient records, appointments, pharmacy, laboratory, billing, and HMO claim submission in one shared database. In 2026, a Nigerian hospital has three honest paths.
  - figure:
    - table:
      - rowgroup:
        - row "Path Cost Range":
          - columnheader "Path"
          - columnheader "Cost Range"
      - rowgroup:
        - row "SaaS for a small clinic ₦150,000 to ₦400,000 a year":
          - rowheader "SaaS for a small clinic"
          - cell "₦150,000 to ₦400,000 a year"
        - row "SaaS for a mid-size hospital ₦1.2M to ₦5M a year":
          - rowheader "SaaS for a mid-size hospital"
          - cell "₦1.2M to ₦5M a year"
        - row "Custom build ₦4M to ₦25M one-time, plus 15 to 20 percent annual maintenance":
          - rowheader "Custom build"
          - cell "₦4M to ₦25M one-time, plus 15 to 20 percent annual maintenance"
  - paragraph: A small clinic running 10 to 20 patients a day rarely needs more than a SaaS plan. A 150-bed multi-specialty hospital with five HMO contracts and an in-house laboratory usually outgrows SaaS within two to three years. The right answer depends on size, claim volume, and how much your workflows differ from a standard template.
  - heading "How Big Is the Nigerian Hospital Market in 2026?" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: Nigeria has roughly 4,000 hospitals, 35,000 primary healthcare centres, and over 50 licensed HMOs as of 2026, according to
    - strong: Federal Ministry of Health
    - text: and
    - strong: NHIA registry data
    - text: . That makes it one of the largest healthcare markets in Africa by absolute size, with significant scope for digitisation.
  - paragraph:
    - text: Healthcare provision is split across public hospitals (federal teaching hospitals, federal medical centres, state general hospitals, and local government PHCs), private hospitals ranging from single-site clinics to multi-site groups, and faith-based hospitals operating under the
    - strong: Christian Health Association of Nigeria
    - text: and other bodies.
  - paragraph: Each layer has different software needs. A private 50-bed hospital wants efficient billing and fast HMO claim turnaround. A teaching hospital needs research-grade record keeping and regulatory reporting. A faith-based mission hospital often needs strong offline capability and lower licence costs.
  - paragraph: A primary healthcare centre needs a lightweight EMR with mother-and-child registers, immunisation records, and reporting into District Health Information System (DHIS2) where applicable.
  - paragraph: Identifying which layer your facility belongs to saves months of evaluating tools that were never going to fit.
  - heading "The Seven Modules That Run a Modern Hospital" [level=2]
  - paragraph: "A complete HMS runs seven modules from one shared database: electronic health records, appointment scheduling, pharmacy and inventory, laboratory information, billing and HMO claims, telemedicine, and reporting. A serious system runs all seven from one shared database."
  - paragraph: A weak system stitches together separate tools, and the gaps show up in billing, reporting, and patient safety.
  - heading "Electronic health records (EHR/EMR)" [level=3]
  - paragraph: The clinical foundation of the system. It holds the patient's full history, including vitals, diagnoses, prescriptions, lab orders, and clinical notes. Doctors should be able to pull any patient's record in under five seconds from any consulting room. Records should be coded to ICD-10 for diagnoses and, where supported, SNOMED CT for clinical terminology.
  - heading "Appointment scheduling and queue management" [level=3]
  - paragraph: Patients book online, by phone, or through WhatsApp. The system schedules across doctors, consulting rooms, and equipment, and shows the front desk a real-time queue with expected wait times. A well-built scheduling module cuts no-show rates and reduces idle time between consultations.
  - heading "Pharmacy and inventory" [level=3]
  - paragraph: The pharmacy module tracks every drug from delivery to dispensing, flags expiries, manages reorder points, and links to the patient's prescription so dispensing is a single action rather than three paper forms. NAFDAC product codes should be supported so the correct drug is verified at the point of dispensing.
  - heading "Laboratory information system" [level=3]
  - paragraph: The laboratory module receives orders from doctors, tracks samples from collection to analysis, captures results, and pushes signed reports back into the patient's EHR without a paper runner. Direct integration with reference laboratories cuts hours of manual data entry per day.
  - heading "Billing, payments, and HMO claims" [level=3]
  - paragraph: The billing module captures every chargeable item across the patient's visit or stay, generates invoices, processes payments through Paystack, Flutterwave, Monnify, or Remita, and submits claims to NHIA, State Health Insurance Schemes, and HMOs in the format each requires. This module has the biggest effect on cash flow.
  - heading "Telemedicine" [level=3]
  - paragraph: Video consultations, follow-up appointments, and second opinions, with consultation notes saved directly to the EHR. Operations should follow the National Telemedicine Guidelines published by the Federal Ministry of Health, and all consultations must be conducted by MDCN-registered practitioners with the practitioner's ID attached to the clinical record.
  - heading "Reporting and clinical analytics" [level=3]
  - paragraph: Live dashboards for the medical director and finance lead, covering patient volume, revenue, claim status, drug stock, and staff productivity. Where required, the system should export data into DHIS2 format for public health reporting.

  - paragraph:

  - paragraph: Buy SaaS if you run a single clinic or small hospital with standard workflows. Build custom if you have specialty workflows, multiple sites, deep HMO integration needs, or you want full ownership of the codebase. Start with open source if you have an in-house technical team or a long-term technical partner. The reasoning behind each path follows.
  - heading "Buy a SaaS platform" [level=3]
  - paragraph: The right choice if you run a single clinic or a small hospital with standard workflows, your team is small, and you do not have specialty needs that a generic platform cannot cover. You get the system live in weeks rather than months, and the vendor handles updates, hosting, and security.
  - heading "Build custom" [level=3]
  - paragraph: The right choice if you have specialty workflows, multiple sites, deep HMO and NHIA integration requirements, or a high volume of insured-patient claims. Teaching hospitals, large multi-site groups, and HMO carriers consistently choose this route. Full data ownership and a codebase you control are additional reasons to build.

OpenMRS is a serious open-source EHR used in over 40 countries with a strong global community and a growing presence in African healthcare systems. The cost model shifts from licence fees to engineering, hosting, and maintenance, but the data and the codebase stay entirely yours.
